sections.h2: How fast can I sell a house in Estero, FL?
sections.html:
A cash sale in Estero can close as quickly as the title work allows, because there is no lender appraisal or loan approval to wait for. The slower parts are payoffs, liens and any owner who has to sign from out of state.

Estero is a village in Lee County, Florida. If your home belongs to a homeowners association, ask early whether it needs to issue a payoff or approval letter, since that request can add days to a closing.

Below you will find how Estero came to be a village, the Lee County homestead facts that matter after a sale, and the state costs and deadlines tied to the deed.

sections.h2: What is Estero's history and how is it governed?
sections.html:
Estero took its name from the Spanish word for estuary, and early settlement clustered along the Estero River. According to the village's own history page, the first homesteader, Gustave Damkohler, farmed citrus there in 1882, and the Koreshan Unity under Cyrus Teed began settling the river area in 1894. Eleven of the Koreshans' remaining historic structures are kept at the Koreshan State Historic Site.

A short-lived Town of Estero was incorporated in 1904 and abolished in 1907. The modern village came much later. Community leaders started incorporation efforts in July 2013, residents signed 10,238 petitions, and the Lee County Legislative Delegation approved a local bill for a referendum on the November 4, 2014 ballot. About 86 percent of voters said yes, and the Village of Estero was created on December 31, 2014, covering roughly 20 square miles.

For sellers, the useful point is that Estero is its own municipality with a village government, while the property appraiser, tax collector and clerk are Lee County offices. Your deed is recorded in Lee County, and your tax bill comes from the county.

sections.h2: What does the Lee County Property Appraiser say about homestead after a sale?
sections.html:
The Lee County Property Appraiser prints that the state's deadline to apply for exemptions is March 1 and that exemptions are not granted retroactively. Its page also shows the 2026 homestead benefit, with the first $25,000 applying to all taxes and an additional amount of up to $26,411 applying only to non-school taxes on assessed value above $50,000.

When you sell, your exemption stops. The buyer must file their own application with the appraiser. If you move within Florida, portability can carry part of your Save Our Homes benefit to the new home when you apply by March 1.

  • A seller who rents the house out before closing can lose the homestead for that year.
  • A buyer who purchases after January 1 should file by the next March 1.
  • Ask the appraiser's exemption staff to confirm status on the property record before closing.

sections.h2: Does Estero offer a senior exemption on top of homestead?
sections.html:
Yes. The Lee County Property Appraiser lists the Village of Estero among the local governments that have approved the senior exemption for owners 65 and older with limited household income. Its page shows $50,000 and up to $250,000 for the Village of Estero, the same figure printed for all Lee County millages.

The application is due by March 1, and if you do not have your income paperwork by then, the office says to apply anyway because the deadline to supply the income information is June 1. At least one applicant must be 65 or older on January 1 of the assessment year. A buyer who qualifies may want to ask whether that benefit changes their expected tax bill, which matters if you are selling to an older owner-occupant.

sections.h2: What does the Save Our Homes reset mean for an Estero buyer?
sections.html:
Florida's Save Our Homes cap limits annual assessment increases for a homestead to the lower of 3 percent or the inflation change, and the Department of Revenue prints cap figures of 2.7 percent for 2026 and 2.9 percent for 2025. A sale ends that protection for the seller's property. The state says a change of ownership returns the property to just value on the following January 1.

This is why buyers sometimes see a tax bill that is higher than the seller's was. If you have owned your Estero home for many years, your assessed value is probably below its market value. A buyer who knows this can plan for it, and a seller who explains the timing can head off a late surprise at closing.

sections.h2: What closing costs and deadlines apply to an Estero sale?
sections.html:
The deed tax for Lee County is 70 cents per $100 of consideration under section 201.02, and the Department of Revenue says all parties are liable for it regardless of who agrees to pay. The clerk collects the tax at recording. Recording charges follow section 28.24, which lists $5.00 for the first page and $4.00 for each additional page, plus technology and trust fund charges.

On the tax calendar, Florida mails the notice of proposed taxes in August, sends bills in November, and treats unpaid taxes as delinquent on April 1. If you are selling in the fall or winter, ask the title company how the bill will be prorated.

  1. Request payoffs for any mortgage or lien.
  2. Ask your homeowners association for a payoff or estoppel letter.
  3. Confirm the tax status with the Lee County Tax Collector.
  4. Review the deed and sign it in front of two witnesses.

sections.h2: What if I inherited the Estero house?
sections.html:
An inherited house can usually be sold once the court or the estate gives someone authority to sign. Florida allows summary administration when the non-exempt estate is $150,000 or less, or when the decedent has been dead more than two years. Creditor claims are barred unless filed by the later of three months after the first publication of the notice to creditors or 30 days after service on a creditor who must be served.

Florida has no state estate tax for people who died after December 31, 2004. A personal representative's deed under a probated will is listed as not subject to doc stamps. Talk to a probate attorney or the Lee County Clerk's probate office about which path fits your estate.

faqs.q: Is Estero a city or part of Lee County?
faqs.a: Estero is a village created on December 31, 2014, and it sits inside Lee County. The county's property appraiser, tax collector and clerk still handle your tax roll, bill and recording.

faqs.q: When must a new owner apply for homestead?
faqs.a: By March 1 of the tax year they want the exemption. Lee County says exemptions are not granted retroactively, so file as soon as you move in.

faqs.q: Does the senior exemption apply in Estero?
faqs.a: Yes, for owners 65 and older with limited household income. The appraiser's page prints $50,000 and up to $250,000 for the Village of Estero, with a March 1 application deadline and a June 1 deadline for income papers.

faqs.q: Do I need a lawyer to sell an inherited house?
faqs.a: Not always. Small estates may qualify for summary administration, but title companies often need court paperwork or a personal representative's authority. A probate attorney can tell you which applies.

faqs.q: How much is the deed tax in Estero?
faqs.a: The state rate in Lee County is 70 cents for each $100 of consideration, as printed by the Department of Revenue. The clerk collects it at recording.
